_comment: Shared club model definitions. Each owned club is a ClubInstance referencing one of these by id. Modifiers are multipliers around the stock launch numbers (distance = ball speed, spin = backspin, forgiveness scales off-centre penalties, control scales heel/toe shot shaping, dispersion_deg is random push at a full mishit). base_value is the fair used value in dollars at Good condition. slot is the bag slot (IRONS covers 4I..9I). Putters flagged collectible are the seven-piece prestige collection: exactly seven. Illegal clubs are admin sandbox only.

models.name: Daddy's Driver
models.desc: Clubhouse rental. Scuffed crown, does the job.

models.name: Daddy's 3 Wood
models.desc: Rental fairway wood with a rattle.

models.name: Daddy's 5 Wood
models.desc: Rental five wood. Grip is shiny.

models.name: Daddy's Irons 4-9
models.desc: Mixed rental iron set, two of them from a different set entirely.

models.name: Daddy's Pitching Wedge
models.desc: Rental pitching wedge.

models.name: Daddy's Gap Wedge
models.desc: Rental gap wedge.

models.name: Daddy's Sand Wedge
models.desc: Rental sand wedge, grooves half gone.

models.name: Daddy's Lob Wedge
models.desc: Rental lob wedge.

models.name: Daddy's Putter
models.desc: Rental blade with a bent shaft label.

models.name: Thrift Titan 460
models.desc: Big, friendly, a little dead off the face. Forgives more than it rewards.
models.tell: Sticker residue on the sole.

models.name: Slice Slayer Offset
models.desc: Draw-biased game improver. Straightens you out and costs you yards.
models.tell: Offset hosel, the cure for a slice.

models.name: Persimmon Ghost
models.desc: Real wood, real insert, real consequences. Shapes shots like a dream on the sweet spot.
models.tell: Brass sole plate, oiled grain.

models.name: Rocket Boomer LT
models.desc: Low-spin cannon from the illegal-face era. Nukes the sweet spot, punishes everything else.
models.tell: Hot face, thin crown. The old ones go.

models.name: Hollow Point Tour
models.desc: A tour-department head with weights you cannot buy. Long and eerily quiet.
models.tell: Serial stamped on the hosel, no retail sticker.

models.name: Meteor XR Prototype
models.desc: Pre-production carbon head that never shipped. The distance is real.
models.tell: Hand-written loft on masking tape. Raw carbon crown.

models.name: Garage Sale 3 Wood
models.desc: Ubiquitous, unloved, fine.
models.tell: Grip tape showing.

models.name: Steelhead Classic 3W
models.desc: Everybody's dad's favorite fairway wood, for good reason.
models.tell: Classic steel crown, unmistakable pear shape.

models.name: Tour Spoon 13
models.desc: Compact, hot, unforgiving. Off the deck it is a weapon in the right hands.
models.tell: Tiny head, tour weight port.

models.name: Lowball 5 Wood
models.desc: Easy launch, no drama.
models.tell: Chipped paint on the toe.

models.name: Heirloom 5 Wood
models.desc: Laminated maple from a workshop that closed decades ago. Flies high, lands soft.
models.tell: Maker's mark burned into the crown.

models.name: Rescue Rookie 3H
models.desc: Replaces a long iron you never hit well anyway.
models.tell: Loft sticker half-peeled.

models.name: Cloudcutter 4H
models.desc: High launch, soft landing, forgiving from the rough.
models.tell: Deep face, faint alignment line.

models.name: Utility Iron 2U
models.desc: Driving iron for windy days. Piercing flight, zero help.
models.tell: Hollow-body seam, tour-only loft.

models.name: Thrift Cavity Backs 4-9
models.desc: Chunky, forgiving, slightly short. A fine set to learn on.
models.tell: One iron is a different model entirely.

models.name: Mustard Muscle Backs 4-9
models.desc: Yellowed ferrules and butter-soft forging. Rewards a good strike.
models.tell: Forged stamp on the hosel.

models.name: Game Improver XL 4-9
models.desc: Wide soles, strong lofts, flies far and stops nowhere.
models.tell: Sole as wide as a spatula.

models.name: Blade Runner Forged 4-9
models.desc: Thin topline, tiny sweet spot, absolute control when you find it.
models.tell: Satin finish, raw leading edge.

models.name: Tour Forged CB 4-9
models.desc: Players' cavity back from a tour van. The best of both.
models.tell: Tour-van engraving under the grime.

models.name: Combo Set Prototype 4-9
models.desc: Hollow long irons blended into forged short irons. Never made it to retail.
models.tell: Hand-stamped PROTO in each cavity.

models.name: Grocery Store PW
models.desc: Came in a boxed set next to the cereal.
models.tell: Barcode on the shaft.

models.name: Bent Neck PW
models.desc: Bent a degree strong by a fitter who knew what they were doing.
models.tell: Loft written on the hosel in paint pen.

models.name: Rusty Gap 52
models.desc: Raw steel gone orange. Grabs the ball hard, punishes fat contact.
models.tell: Rust is the finish, not a flaw.

models.name: Flop Master 60
models.desc: High bounce, wide sole, opens up like a door.
models.tell: Face grooves still sharp.

models.name: Raw Face 56
models.desc: Unplated face, milled grooves. Spins like a top, no help on a thin one.
models.tell: Face rusts on purpose. Milling marks visible.

models.name: Tour Grind 58
models.desc: Hand-ground sole for one player's swing. Happens to like yours.
models.tell: Grinder marks on the heel, tour stamp.

models.name: Sand Shovel SW
models.desc: Enormous sole. Gets out of the bunker, then stops helping.
models.tell: Sole wider than the face.

models.name: Rustbelt Blade
models.feel: Clicky and honest. You hear every putt.
models.desc: A battered blade with surprising charm. Pitted, orange, and somehow always on line.
models.tell: Rust follows the sweet spot exactly.

models.name: Brass Relic
models.feel: Heavy and soft. Rolls the ball early.
models.desc: An old brass putter with distinctive patina. Heavy head, thin flange, green in the corners.
models.tell: Patina is even, never polished.

models.name: Midnight Mallet
models.feel: Muted thud. Hard to twist, easy to trust.
models.desc: A dark mallet with bold alignment markings. Three white lines you could land a plane on.
models.tell: Alignment lines still crisp under the dust.

models.name: Copper Classic
models.desc: An elegant copper-finish collector piece. Heel-toe weighting, plumber's neck, ridiculous glow at sunset.
models.tell: Solid copper, not plating. No wear-through anywhere.

models.name: Tourline Prototype
models.desc: An unusual prototype with a recognizable silhouette. Winged, raw, a blue sightline nobody else has.
models.tell: No model name anywhere. Just a number.

models.name: Blackout Tour Issue
models.desc: A scarce tour-style collectible with premium detailing. Matte black, red sightline, a weight kit you cannot buy.
models.tell: Circle stamp hidden under the grip edge.

models.name: Scotty Cameron - The Grail
models.desc: The ultimate rare find and collection centerpiece. Newport shape, cherry dots, and a headcover worth more than most bags.
models.tell: Three cherry-red dots. Milled face. Somebody didn't know.

models.name: Grenade Prototype Driver
models.desc: ADMIN SANDBOX. A BombTech-Grenade-inspired novelty head that hits 400-yard bombs and detonates on contact. Not legal anywhere, including here.

models.name: Auto-Putt 9000
models.desc: ADMIN SANDBOX. Reads the green, picks the line, sets the pace, sinks it inside its range. Not a collectible. Not even a little.
